plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 27: Biomolecules: Lipids
plan.contextChunk: This figure sets a three-dimensional rendering of a lipid bilayer beside the flat structural formula of the molecule that builds it. On the left, a slab of membrane is drawn in perspective with a stepped cutaway at one corner: rows of small green spheres tile the top and bottom faces, and the interior between them is packed with pale tan wavy strands that meet tip to tip along the slab's midplane, so the two leaflets face each other tails inward. On the right, a glycerophospholipid is drawn with a vertical glycerol backbone reading CH2, CH, CH2 from top to bottom. The topmost branch is printed in green and reads CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH2N(CH3)3+, tagged by a green arrow labeled "Ionic head". The two lower branches each run through O-C(=O) into a long tan ribbon of the same shade and waviness as the strands filling the slab, and a magenta label "Nonpolar tails" sends two arrows to their free ends. Matching the green and tan across the two halves lets the reader place each region of the drawn molecule at its position in the assembled sheet. The pairing accounts for how a long nonpolar tail bound to a polar ionic head drives aggregation into a bilayer that keeps hydrocarbon away from water.

demo_steps.title: Polar surface
demo_steps.narration: The green ionic head in the structural formula matches the green spheres covering both outer faces of the bilayer. These charged groups are positioned where the membrane contacts water.

demo_steps.title: Linker layer
demo_steps.narration: The glycerol backbone and ester linkages sit between the head group and the hydrocarbon chains. In the bilayer they form thin interfacial bands just under each head-group layer.

demo_steps.title: Hydrophobic interior
demo_steps.narration: The two tan nonpolar tails in one molecule correspond to the tan wavy strands filling the slab interior. At the middle of the bilayer, tails from opposite leaflets meet tip-to-tip.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Overall layout should match the source: membrane slab on the left, structural formula on the right, both visible in one wide frame. World scale: bilayer centered near x=-3.2, y=0, z=0; membrane plane runs mainly along X and Z, thickness runs along Y. Slab approximately 3.8 units long in X, 1.45 units thick in Y, and 1.55 units deep in Z. Orient the slab so its long axis reads left-to-right on screen, its depth recedes up/right, and the top face plus front/side cutaway are visible. Use a stepped missing corner near the front-left/top edge to expose the tan interior, echoing the source cutaway. Head spheres: radius about 0.095 units, arranged in staggered grids, about 14 columns by 7 rows on the top leaflet at y=+0.72 and bottom leaflet at y=-0.72; green gradient around #39c987 with darker outlines/shadows #119b63. Nonpolar tails: pale salmon/tan #c98a7a to #d5a094, wavy tube or ribbon curves radius about 0.025 to 0.035; upper leaflet tails start just under top head layer around y=+0.55 and point downward to the midplane y=0, lower leaflet tails start around y=-0.55 and point upward to y=0. Make tails densely packed and vertically wavy, not straight. Glycerol-linker regions in the slab are narrow darker tan/gray-brown bands at y≈+0.55 and y≈-0.55 immediately inside the head spheres. Right structural formula is a camera-facing flat panel centered around x=1.4 to x=5.5, y=-0.1, z=0. Glycerol backbone is vertical: top CH2 at y≈1.05, middle CH at y≈0.2, bottom CH2 at y≈-0.75, with black vertical bonds. Top green branch runs horizontally right from the top CH2 and reads CH2-O-P(=O)(O−)-O-CH2CH2N+(CH3)3; use green #008c5a for this whole branch and the Ionic head label. Upper tail branch leaves the middle CH through O-C(=O) and becomes a long tan wavy horizontal tail at y≈0.15 extending to the far right. Lower tail branch leaves the bottom CH2 through O-C(=O) and becomes a second tan wavy horizontal tail at y≈-1.05. Nonpolar tails label is magenta #ff1493 on the far right, with two magenta arrows angled leftward to the free ends of both tails. The ionic-head label sits above the green branch with a green arrow angled down-left toward the choline/phosphate region. The glycerol linker highlight should include the vertical CH2-CH-CH2 backbone and both ester O-C(=O) connectors, plus the two interfacial linker bands in the bilayer.
interactionPlan.notes: Use instanced spheres for bilayer heads and CatmullRomCurve3 tube/ribbon geometry for hydrocarbon tails. Render the structural formula as flat text sprites/SDF text plus thin cylinder or line bonds on a camera-facing plane so it resembles the printed 2D formula. Click picking should group objects into exactly three selectable regions: ionic head, glycerol linker, nonpolar tails; clicking either the formula or the slab updates the same highlight state as the mappingFocus toggle. Highlight selected regions with a soft emissive outline/glow while dimming unselected regions slightly. Implement cutawayDepth as a horizontal clipping or reveal plane moving from the upper surface through y=0 to the lower surface; show the active slice plane as a translucent pale blue sheet with a thin outline. Keep the camera mostly fixed to preserve the textbook composition rather than encouraging free orbit.

authoredContext:
Phospholipids are found widely in both plant and animal tissues and make up approximately 50% to 60% of cell membranes. Because they are like soaps in having a long, nonpolar hydrocarbon tail bound to a polar ionic head, phospholipids in the cell membrane organize into a lipid bilayer about 5.0 nm (50 Å) thick. As shown in the figure, the nonpolar tails aggregate in the center of the bilayer in much the same way that soap tails aggregate in the center of a micelle. This bilayer serves as an effective barrier to the passage of water, ions, and other components into and out of cells.

Aggregation of glycerophospholipids into the lipid bilayer that composes cell membranes.

Glycerophospholipids combine with the lipid bilayer comprising a cell membrane. An arrow points to the ionic head and two nonpolar tails of the lipid bilayer.

discrepancies: The structural formula is shown obliquely with the two hydrocarbon tails slanting downward, whereas the source has a flat front-on chemical diagram with nearly horizontal parallel tails.
Most non-selected molecule atoms, bonds, tails, and the 'Nonpolar tails' label are faded by the default highlight state, but the source shows all parts at full contrast.
An extra translucent blue cutaway plane and highlight/halo effects are present in the bilayer, which do not appear in the source figure.

The bilayer and molecule are scaled and spaced differently from the source: the generated content is smaller and more spread out, with the right chemical structure less dominant and less textbook-like.
The bilayer interior appears more transparent and layered with added bands, while the source shows a denser tan hydrophobic interior beneath the green head groups.
Chemical details such as the ester/carbonyl bonds and glycerol backbone are harder to read and less cleanly arranged than in the original 2D structural formula.
evaluation.notes: The main phospholipid bilayer and labeled molecule are recognizable and the interactions are useful, but the default view, fading, extra cutaway plane, and slanted chemical formula reduce fidelity to the source.
action_items: Reorient the structural formula to be front-facing and keep the two nonpolar tails nearly horizontal and parallel as in the source.
Do not fade non-selected chemical labels and bonds by default; use outlines or subtle highlights instead so all source labels remain readable.
Hide or remove the translucent blue cutaway plane and halo effects in the default view.
Resize and reposition the bilayer and molecule to better match the original side-by-side composition, with a larger clean chemical diagram on the right.
plan_action_items: Use a composition plan with an axonometric 3D bilayer on the left and a flat front-on structural formula on the right, rather than placing both under the same oblique perspective camera.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interactions are strong, while the issues are mainly implementation-level camera/layout, scale, default highlighting, and removal of hallucinated visual effects that the generator can fix.

demo_steps.title: Polar surface
demo_steps.narration: The green ionic head in the structural formula matches the green spheres covering both outer faces of the bilayer. These charged groups are positioned where the membrane contacts water.

demo_steps.title: Linker layer
demo_steps.narration: The glycerol backbone and ester linkages sit between the head group and the hydrocarbon chains. In the bilayer they form thin interfacial bands just under each head-group layer.

demo_steps.title: Hydrophobic interior
demo_steps.narration: The two tan nonpolar tails in one molecule correspond to the tan wavy strands filling the slab interior. At the middle of the bilayer, tails from opposite leaflets meet tip-to-tip.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Overall layout should match the source: membrane slab on the left, structural formula on the right, both visible in one wide frame. World scale: bilayer centered near x=-3.2, y=0, z=0; membrane plane runs mainly along X and Z, thickness runs along Y. Slab approximately 3.8 units long in X, 1.45 units thick in Y, and 1.55 units deep in Z. Orient the slab so its long axis reads left-to-right on screen, its depth recedes up/right, and the top face plus front/side cutaway are visible. Use a stepped missing corner near the front-left/top edge to expose the tan interior, echoing the source cutaway. Head spheres: radius about 0.095 units, arranged in staggered grids, about 14 columns by 7 rows on the top leaflet at y=+0.72 and bottom leaflet at y=-0.72; green gradient around #39c987 with darker outlines/shadows #119b63. Nonpolar tails: pale salmon/tan #c98a7a to #d5a094, wavy tube or ribbon curves radius about 0.025 to 0.035; upper leaflet tails start just under top head layer around y=+0.55 and point downward to the midplane y=0, lower leaflet tails start around y=-0.55 and point upward to y=0. Make tails densely packed and vertically wavy, not straight. Glycerol-linker regions in the slab are narrow darker tan/gray-brown bands at y≈+0.55 and y≈-0.55 immediately inside the head spheres. Right structural formula is a camera-facing flat panel centered around x=1.4 to x=5.5, y=-0.1, z=0. Glycerol backbone is vertical: top CH2 at y≈1.05, middle CH at y≈0.2, bottom CH2 at y≈-0.75, with black vertical bonds. Top green branch runs horizontally right from the top CH2 and reads CH2-O-P(=O)(O−)-O-CH2CH2N+(CH3)3; use green #008c5a for this whole branch and the Ionic head label. Upper tail branch leaves the middle CH through O-C(=O) and becomes a long tan wavy horizontal tail at y≈0.15 extending to the far right. Lower tail branch leaves the bottom CH2 through O-C(=O) and becomes a second tan wavy horizontal tail at y≈-1.05. Nonpolar tails label is magenta #ff1493 on the far right, with two magenta arrows angled leftward to the free ends of both tails. The ionic-head label sits above the green branch with a green arrow angled down-left toward the choline/phosphate region. The glycerol linker highlight should include the vertical CH2-CH-CH2 backbone and both ester O-C(=O) connectors, plus the two interfacial linker bands in the bilayer.
interactionPlan.notes: Use instanced spheres for bilayer heads and CatmullRomCurve3 tube/ribbon geometry for hydrocarbon tails. Render the structural formula as flat text sprites/SDF text plus thin cylinder or line bonds on a camera-facing plane so it resembles the printed 2D formula. Click picking should group objects into exactly three selectable regions: ionic head, glycerol linker, nonpolar tails; clicking either the formula or the slab updates the same highlight state as the mappingFocus toggle. Highlight selected regions with a soft emissive outline/glow while dimming unselected regions slightly. Implement cutawayDepth as a horizontal clipping or reveal plane moving from the upper surface through y=0 to the lower surface; show the active slice plane as a translucent pale blue sheet with a thin outline. Keep the camera mostly fixed to preserve the textbook composition rather than encouraging free orbit.
